label: Studio quick edit drawer
description: A non-modal panel docked to the right edge of Studio, 550px wide, opened by clicking the body of a Catalog result row. It shares its shell with Explorer's quick view (the same 550px dialog, the same inset of 70px 0 0 0, the same suppressed backdrop) and carries a different body: the title is editable in place, the properties are editable fields rather than read-only pairs, and two of the four tabs exist to assign people and to moderate suggestions. The page behind it stays live, so the clicked row keeps its highlight and the filter rail keeps working.
when: Use when a Studio user needs to inspect or correct one catalog item without losing the result list they found it in. Do NOT use the Explorer capture `right-sliding-drawer`, which is a DIFFERENT RECIPE for the same pattern, not a different pattern: this recipe declares `right-sliding-drawer` too, and the selector tells the two apart by `apps`. That capture is Explorer's quick VIEW of the same shell. Its body is read-only, it carries a favourite button Studio does not have, and it puts result counts on its tab labels where Studio's carry none. Explorer's five tabs read `Description`, `Fields 7`, `Properties 19`, `Contacts 9`, `Suggestions 1` on the captured item, so the count is on four of the five and `Description` leads; Studio's four are `General`, `Properties`, `People`, `Suggestions`. Both apps carry Properties and Suggestions, so a Suggestions tab does NOT tell the two apart. Both drawers were captured on the same host, `manufacturing.zeenea.app`, on 2026-09-30, so the differences are between the apps and not between two environments. Do NOT use asset-detail-360: that is the full item page this drawer previews, reached by clicking the item TITLE rather than the row body. Do NOT use a modal: the product renders this as a drawer deliberately, and the stylesheet says so, `.zng-drawer::backdrop { display: none }` against `.zng-dialog::backdrop` at 60 percent black. A modal would take the list away, which is the one thing this surface exists to preserve.

derivedFrom.surface: Studio > Catalog > result row body > quick edit drawer

slots.header: A row holding the item type tag, the Shared tag and the item name, and exactly TWO icon buttons: open in full page (view-detail, a link to the item route) and close. Explorer's equivalent carries three, the extra one being favourite.
slots.subtitle: 'Technical name: …', then 'Catalog: … / Data Product: … / Connection: …' (data product and connection are links), then 'Stage:' with the lifecycle stage tag, which opens a menu to move the stage.
slots.metrics: A three-up strip of label-over-value pairs: Last updated with a date, the linked items (Fields on a Dataset) with a count rendered as a link, and Completion with a progress bar and its percentage.
slots.tabs: Four tabs of equal width, General, Properties, People and Suggestions, carrying NO counts on their labels. General is active when the drawer opens.
slots.tab-general: A 'Glossary Items' heading with its count in parentheses over a multi-select of removable chips, then a 'Description' heading with an information icon over the item's description, then 'Source Description' ("No source description" when the source gives none).
slots.tab-properties: Property groups, each introduced by an uppercase group heading such as GENERAL, over label-and-field pairs. The fields are mixed and mostly editable: read-only text, an external link, an empty combo box prompting 'Add <property>', and a multi-select field holding removable chips with a clear-all control.
slots.tab-people: Two role sections, Curator and Contact, each headed by its label with an assign-person icon button at the right edge. A filled role draws an avatar chip carrying initials, the person's name and their job title on a second line, plus a remove control. An empty role draws an empty state, illustration over the sentence 'No curator has been assigned.'
slots.tab-suggestions: A segmented control filtering by suggestion state, Accepted, Rejected, Pending and All, with Pending selected by default, over the matching suggestions. When none match it draws an empty state reading 'There are no suggestions for this filter.'

renderNotes: The `drawer-header` section splices to one FRAME that is simultaneously this recipe's `header`, `subtitle` and `metrics` regions (title row, catalog line, metric strip are its children, not separate roots); its SECTION node's `slot` is therefore an array (`["header", "subtitle", "metrics"]`), stamped onto that one FRAME rather than split across three.

Children of a VERTICAL frame must omit `sizing`. `sizing.horizontal: "FILL"` emits `flex:1`, which in a column container distributes height instead of hugging content, while width already fills from flexbox's stretch default. `tests/app-context-recipes.test.js` walks every skeleton for this case.

This recipe composes the overlay surface ONLY, at its captured width of 550px. In the product the dialog is `position: fixed` with `inset: 70px 0 0 0` and `z-index: 950`, so it docks to the right edge BELOW the global app header rather than over it, and it is opened non-modally: `dialog.matches(':modal')` is false and `.zng-drawer::backdrop` is `display: none`. Compose the page behind it from `faceted-browse` when a full screen is wanted.

Every value is the captured drawer's (COUNT BY ORDER STATUS, opened from the Studio Catalog, manufacturing.zeenea.app, 2026-09-30). The drawer-header section is shared; this page gives it its values through the SECTION node's `values`.
Studio's drawer tabs carry no counts, unlike Explorer's.

The DS `drawer` component is not used as the shell: its panel takes text only (`Content`), so the General tab's select and headings cannot sit inside it, and it prints "Category:" where the product says "Data Product:". The shell is a plain FRAME at the captured width.
The Properties, People and Suggestions panels are described in `slots`, not drawn: the capture shows General.

children.content: COUNT BY ORDER STATUS is a summary dataset sourced from the connPowerBI connection. It aggregates orders by their current status, providing a high-level operational view of order pipeline distribution.
